payload.title: Two chain stages on a shared shaft

model.title: Two chain stages on a shared shaft
model.description: Unqualified teaching proposal for human review: steady ideal chain transmission with independently adjustable tooth counts and a rigid intermediate shaft.
assumptions: Input domains and illustrative defaults: stage1_driver_teeth=40 and stage2_driver_teeth=40, each restricted to {32,40,48}; stage1_driven_teeth=20 and stage2_driven_teeth=20, each restricted to {16,20,28}.
input_frequency ranges from 0 to 2 Hz, default 1 Hz. Display this control as input cadence from 0 to 120 rpm using display multiplier 60.
Each open chain connects only its own driving and driven sprockets. Parallel shafts rotate in the same direction, with positive rotation viewed from the same side.
The first driven sprocket and second driving sprocket are rigidly attached to one intermediate shaft. Bind both rotations and their readouts to intermediate_frequency.
The illustrative chain pitch is fixed at 0.0127 m for both stages; it is not a product specification.
Use equivalent smooth sprocket radii N*p/(2*pi) for mean-motion teaching geometry, not tooth-accurate pitch circles. Mean chain speed is N*p*f.
For later layout, shaft axes run along +z; shaft centres lie along +x. The two chain stages occupy separate z planes. Layout distances are teaching choices.
This is a steady model: time_experiment=null. Rotational frequencies specify motion rates, not startup dynamics. No initial angular phase is physically prescribed.
All frequency readouts may display rpm using multiplier 60; ratios remain dimensionless. No implicit unit conversion enters the equations.
Across all settings, stage ratios are 8/7 to 3, overall ratio is 64/49 to 9, intermediate frequency is 0 to 6 Hz, and output frequency is 0 to 18 Hz.
Equivalent radii range from 0.032 to 0.098 m; chain speeds range from 0 to 1.2192 m/s for stage 1 and 0 to 3.6576 m/s for stage 2.
limitations: Only steady ideal no-slip kinematics are represented; no torque, loads, road speed, startup dynamics or engineering validation.
No meshing-gear topology, chain elasticity, backlash, chordal speed variation, tooth engagement dynamics or losses are modeled.
Smooth equivalent radii explain mean transmission motion; they do not specify manufacturable sprocket geometry.

definition.title: Two chains, one shared shaft
definition.description: A simplified open bench transmission connects two chain stages through one rigid middle shaft. Initial settings are illustrative defaults.

limits: Steady ideal no-slip kinematics only: no torque, loads, road speed, startup dynamics or engineering validation.
No meshing-gear topology, elasticity, backlash, chordal speed variation, engagement dynamics or losses.
Smooth equivalent radii N*p/(2*pi) represent mean motion, not manufacturable sprocket teeth.
Driver choices are 32, 40 or 48 teeth; driven choices are 16, 20 or 28. Input cadence is 0–120 rpm.
Both middle sprockets and the shared shaft use intermediate_frequency; the output uses output_frequency. Frequency displays use multiplier 60 for rpm.
Uniform visual mapping: 100 scene units per metre. Support dimensions and chain appearance are illustrative assumptions, not product specifications.
Sprocket outer profiles change with equivalent radius while bores and hubs stay unchanged. Both open tangent chain routes follow their respective radii throughout the control domain.

Chain length and physical link count are not predicted. Each selectable chain uses illustrative repeated segments driven by its declared mean chain speed; segments are not individually simulated links in contact with teeth. time_experiment remains null; no startup or elapsed-time experiment is introduced.

parts.label: Bench base
parts.explanation: This thick base keeps the three shaft supports steady.

parts.label: Input bearing housing
parts.explanation: This support holds the bearings around the input shaft.

parts.label: Input front bearing
parts.explanation: A bearing supports a turning shaft with rolling balls inside.

parts.label: Input rear bearing
parts.explanation: This bearing supports the other end of the input shaft.

parts.label: Shared-shaft bearing housing
parts.explanation: This support holds the shaft shared by both stages.

parts.label: Shared-shaft front bearing
parts.explanation: This bearing supports the shared shaft beside the first chain.

parts.label: Shared-shaft rear bearing
parts.explanation: This bearing supports the shared shaft beside the second chain.

parts.label: Output bearing housing
parts.explanation: This support holds the final shaft in place.

parts.label: Output front bearing
parts.explanation: This bearing supports the front end of the output shaft.

parts.label: Output rear bearing
parts.explanation: This bearing supports the output shaft beside the second chain.

parts.label: Input rotating assembly
parts.explanation: The input shaft and its sprocket turn together at the selected cadence.

parts.label: Input shaft
parts.explanation: This shaft brings rotation to the first driving sprocket.

parts.label: First driving hub
parts.explanation: The hub is the thick centre that joins the sprocket to its shaft.

parts.label: Stage 1 driving sprocket
parts.explanation: This wheel pulls the first chain. Its smooth edge represents average chain travel per turn.

parts.label: Rigid shared rotation
parts.explanation: Both middle sprockets share this shaft, so neither can turn faster than the other.

parts.label: Shared intermediate shaft
parts.explanation: This solid shaft joins the first driven sprocket to the second driving sprocket.

parts.label: First driven hub
parts.explanation: This hub locks the first driven sprocket to the shared shaft.

parts.label: Stage 1 driven sprocket
parts.explanation: The first chain turns this sprocket and the shared shaft.

parts.label: Second driving hub
parts.explanation: This hub joins the second driving sprocket to the same shared shaft.

parts.label: Stage 2 driving sprocket
parts.explanation: This sprocket pulls the second chain. It turns at exactly the same rate as the first driven sprocket.

parts.label: Output rotating assembly
parts.explanation: The second chain turns this final shaft and sprocket together.

parts.label: Output shaft
parts.explanation: This shaft carries the final rotation after both chain stages.

parts.label: Final driven hub
parts.explanation: This hub locks the final sprocket to the output shaft.

parts.label: Stage 2 driven sprocket
parts.explanation: The second chain turns this final sprocket. Both stage ratios determine its rotation rate.

parts.label: Stage 1 chain
parts.explanation: This loop carries motion from the input sprocket to the shared shaft.

parts.label: Stage 2 chain
parts.explanation: This separate loop carries motion from the shared shaft to the output sprocket.

experiments.title: Two sprockets, one shaft
experiments.prompt: Predict how both middle sprockets will turn when stage 1 driving teeth changes to 48. Change it, then compare their motion.
experiments.explanation: The first chain turns the first driven sprocket and shared shaft. The second driver is rigidly attached, so both middle sprockets use the same intermediate frequency. Motion is shown at 20× slowdown.

experiments.title: Change the first driven sprocket
experiments.prompt: Predict whether the shared shaft will turn faster or slower with 28 first-stage driven teeth. Change it and compare the stage 1 ratio and motion.
experiments.explanation: Stage 1 speed ratio is driving teeth divided by driven teeth. Increasing driven teeth lowers that ratio and the shared-shaft rate at fixed input cadence.

experiments.title: Change stage 2 alone
experiments.prompt: Predict what changes when the second driver has 32 teeth. Compare the middle sprockets, output motion and stage 2 ratio.
experiments.explanation: Changing the second driver changes stage 2 chain travel per shared-shaft turn. It changes the output rate, but not the shared-shaft rate.

experiments.title: Connect both stage ratios
experiments.prompt: Predict how 16 final driven teeth will affect the overall ratio. Change it, then multiply the two displayed stage ratios and compare.
experiments.explanation: The second chain turns the final sprocket. Overall speed ratio equals stage 1 ratio times stage 2 ratio. These are steady ideal no-slip relationships, not startup or load predictions.

controls.help: More driving teeth increases stage 1 ratio and both downstream rotation rates at fixed input cadence. Default 40 is illustrative.
More driven teeth lowers stage 1 ratio and both downstream rotation rates at fixed input cadence. Default 20 is illustrative.
More driving teeth increases stage 2 ratio and final rotation rate without changing shared-shaft rate. Default 40 is illustrative.
More driven teeth lowers stage 2 ratio and final rotation rate without changing shared-shaft rate. Default 20 is illustrative.
Input cadence scales all rotation rates without changing tooth ratios. Zero stops modeled motion. Default 60 rpm is illustrative.

coverage.explanation: Stage 1 driving teeth changes the displayed stage 1 ratio and shared-shaft frequency. Both middle sprockets inherit the same rotation, representing rigid coupling rather than independent speeds.
Each tooth-count choice changes its displayed stage ratio and the overall ratio. Stage 1 changes intermediate and final motion; stage 2 changes final motion only.
The displayed overall ratio is the calculated product of both displayed stage ratios. Successive chain stages apply those ratios through the shared shaft to final rotation.

outcomes: Identify the first driven sprocket and second driving sprocket as rigidly coupled on the intermediate shaft, so they turn at the same angular speed.
Explore how changing either stage’s sprocket tooth counts changes intermediate and final rotational speeds.
Understand that the overall speed ratio is the product of the two stage speed ratios.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.
